item.title: Pulp Luck Spending
item.description: Category: pulpPulp Cthulhu – Luck‑Spend Options (Quick‑Reference Table) Luck Cost is expressed in the amount of Luck points that must be spent from the character’s (or NPC’s) Luck pool. When a rule says “all Luck points,” the entire remaining pool is consumed. Identify the situation (e.g., you just failed a Sanity roll, or you’re about to die). Find the matching row to see what the Luck spend accomplishes. Check the cost and verify you have enough Luck points. Declare the spend to the Keeper; apply the effect immediately. Feel free to adapt or house‑rule any of these options to suit the tone of your campaign!Back to Shared Rules

item.title: Pulp Combat Damage
item.description: Category: combat Natural Healing – +2 HP per day (Quick Healer talent bumps this to +3 HP/day). First Aid / Medicine Boost – Successful rolls heal +1D4 HP (Extreme success = 4 HP). No Major‑Wound Penalty – Heroes do not suffer the usual major‑wound effects. Death Thresholds Instant death: Single attack ≥ maximum HP. Dying: Single attack ≥ ½ maximum HP and reduces HP to 0. Unconscious: HP drops to 0 (but not ≥ ½ max). Half‑HP Shock: If a single blow cuts HP by ≥ ½ max and leaves the hero above 0, they must make a CON roll to stay conscious. Dying State – Mark current HP as “D” (dying). CON Rolls – Made at the end of each round; any failure = immediate death. Stabilizing First Aid (success) → removes “D”, restores 1D4 HP (Extreme = 4 HP). Extreme Cases (e.g., being ripped apart) may render First Aid impossible – death is inevitable. Follow‑up Medicine – After stabilization, a successful Medicine roll adds another 1D4 HP (Extreme = 4 HP). Base Rate – +2 HP/day (or +3 HP/day with Quick Healer). Medical Assistance – Each successful daily Medicine roll adds 1 HP to that day’s natural healing (total +3 HP). Modifiers – Hospital care may grant a bonus die; unsanitary conditions may impose a penalty die. Failed Medicine – May reduce healing (e.g., lose 1 HP or, on a pushed roll, lose 1D3 HP). Near‑Death Trauma – Typically triggers a Sanity roll (0 or 1 SAN loss depending on outcome). Role‑Playing Hook – Encourage players to describe lingering injuries (broken limbs, missing fingers, etc.) for dramatic effect, but remember pulp heroes can often “brush it off.” Spending Luck – A dying hero may expend all remaining Luck points (minimum 30 LP required) to cheat death. Result of Luck Spend Luck drops to 0. Hero immediately regains 1D6 + 1 HP. Injuries remain; further healing still required. No further CON rolls needed for that death episode. Narrative Requirement – Player must describe how the hero miraculously survives. Max HP = 22, current = 8. Trap deals 18 damage → HP = ‑10 → Dying (≥ ½ max, reduced to 0). First Aid succeeds → “D” removed, 1D4 HP restored (e.g., 3 HP). Medicine roll succeeds → additional 1D4 HP (e.g., 4 HP). Natural healing resumes (+2 HP/day, possibly +1 HP from daily Medicine). Max HP = 34, current = 17. Star‑spawn claw deals 19 damage → HP = ‑2 → Dying (≥ ½ max, reduced to 0). Luck spend (≥ 30 LP) → Luck → 0, regain 1D6 + 1 HP (e.g., 5 HP). CON roll at end of round succeeds → remains conscious. Allies apply First Aid (success) → +1D4 HP (e.g., 3 HP). Daily Medicine rolls add extra HP each day (+1 HP per successful roll). Facing instant death from Cthulhu’s foot, Maximillian spends all 36 Luck (≥ 30). Describes a cinematic survival (e.g., diving behind a shattered column, a gust of wind lifting him). Luck drops to 0, he regains 1D6 + 1 HP, avoids death, and continues the chase. Back to Shared Rules

item.title: Pnakotic Manuscripts
item.description: Category: TomesLanguage: English Author: Unknown author and translator Date: 15th century Five cataloged bound manuscripts survive, each a partial copy of a larger lost work. The precursor Pnakotica was written in classical Greek and may preserve knowledge originating with prehuman crinoid beings. Chant - of - Thoth Call of Cthulhu, “Tomes of Eldritch Lore,” page(s) 233 in the supplied PDF.Back to Shared Rules

item.title: Ancient Roman Pnakotic Scroll
item.description: Category: TomesLanguage: Latin Author and translator: Unknown Date: c. 200 BCE This scroll claims to be a translation from an Etruscan stone tablet. It discusses the crystals of Naphkon, which the ancient Lomarians considered sacred, and details how to create them. The Lomarians used the stones to view distant times, places, and worlds. They could project their psyches—or even those of others—through these stones. A “Great Race” was credited with creating and truly mastering such projection techniques.Back to Shared Rules
